question: Is 1.1.1.1's divergence per-REFERRAL (H1: the unrelated ADDITIONAL is used as the delegation target for the whole delegated subtree) or name-specific (H2)? (final-verdict section 3, O1-fork)
method: Query names UNDER the forged-referral delegation (blog.alice.poc.debiru.net -> external NS ns-33.awsdns-04.com + ADDITIONAL A 157.112.149.243) that were never queried before, plus sibling/control names outside that delegation, on 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8. Ordinary bounded queries.

names_under_forged_delegation.1.1.1.1: NXDOMAIN with SOA MNAME ns1.static.ne.jp / RNAME root.static.ne.jp for blog.alice.poc.debiru.net — i.e. the negative answer came from the ADDITIONAL-supplied endpoint (157.112.149.243, PTR ns1.static.ne.jp), not from the real authority
names_under_forged_delegation.8.8.8.8: NXDOMAIN without the fake zone's SOA (see raw; authority section empty/different)
names_under_forged_delegation.conclusion: 1.1.1.1 walked the forged referral for EVERY name under the delegation, including negative (NXDOMAIN) paths. Combined with the blog-name answer case (85.131.199.2), the divergence is DELEGATION-LEVEL (per-referral), not name-specific.

controls_outside_delegation.result: NXDOMAIN with SOA ns.lavoscore.org on both resolvers — no divergence outside the forged delegation

true_reference.result: blog.bob resolves to 162.43.9.153 on BOTH resolvers (the TRUE server per the author's published description); no divergence

hypothesis_status.H1_additional_as_delegation_target: SUPPORTED — divergence applies to the whole delegated subtree (answer + negative paths) at 1.1.1.1
hypothesis_status.residual: Mechanism still unidentified at implementation level (why only 1.1.1.1; exact code path). The lab matrix's 10 RE-RESOLVE-REAL cells were stub-mediated and did not exercise this iterative path (final-verdict section 3) — lab-matrix is re-running P3 with a non-pre-seeded out-of-bailiwick NS target.

claim_corrections.supersedes: The 'not generalized to arbitrary names' correction in artifacts/dns-reprobe2-2026-10-27.json and downstream docs was itself based on a flawed control: fresh random names were OUTSIDE the blog delegation (under alice.poc.debiru.net directly), so they never walked the forged referral. The correct statement: steering applies to all names under the forged delegation (answer case blog; negative case www/disc1/disc2 via the fake endpoint's SOA), and does not apply outside it (controls).
